A child ran past, laughing, chasing a kite that fluttered like a nervous bird.

and thought, “That’s decent.” 

The wind turned, gentle enough to ruffle his hair, 
cool enough to remind him he was alive. 
He closed his eyes, let the moment settle, 
like tea steeping, slow and unhurried.

soft, the kind that pats the pavement. 
He didn’t rush for shelter. 
He let the droplets kiss his shoulders, 
felt the tiny shock of cold, then warmth from within.

He laughed, not because the jokes were clever,

He thought, maybe it’s not fireworks or grand declarations, 
just a kettle coming gradually to a boil, 
a cat’s head on his lap, a biscuit that crumbles, 
a rain that finds you when you’re not looking.

superhuman eyesight.

a geography of absence I’m too tired to map. 

But the tree will bloom again. 
Its roots remember how to hunger. 
And I, too, will learn the art of mending
not as a cure, but a collage: 
light passing through cracks, painting rainbows 
on walls that once knew only the color of your eyes.

and every step I take 
echoes back a softer version of me 

The night folds around my shoulders 
like a blanket stitched from shadows 
I listen to the whisper of my own heartbeat 
a lone drum in a deserted hall 

No voices answer my questions 
only the rustle of distant leaves 
that tremble against the windowpane 
as if the world itself is holding its breath 

I sit on the edge of a cracked chair 
and stare at the empty space where laughter once lived 
the silence drapes itself over me 
a gentle, uninvited companion 

In this solitude I find a strange comfort 
a room where thoughts can wander free 
where the mind can paint its own horizons 
without the clamor of other eyes 

So I remain, a solitary traveler, 
collecting the quiet moments like fireflies 
and letting their faint glow guide me 
through the endless, hushed night.

The sun, a fiery maestro,

where petals bloom, and scents unfold, 
in a tapestry of color, intricate and bold.

In this grand orchestra, 
each creature plays its part,
a unique and vital instrument, 
that weaves a harmony, a work of art.
The birds, a chorus of songsters, 
trill and chirp, a joyous refrain,
while the bees, a busy ensemble, 
hum and buzz, a soothing strain.

The earth, a vast and gentle mother, 
nourishes and sustains, 
a web of life, where every thread 
is connected, and every strand remains.
In this great symphony of nature, 
we find our place, our voice, our part,
a small but vital instrument, 
that beats with love, and resonates with heart.

So let us listen to the music, 
of the wild and free,
and find our own wild melody, 
in harmony with nature, wild and carefree.
For in the symphony of the earth, 
we find our own true voice,
a voice that whispers, wild and low, 
of the beauty, wonder, and joy, that makes us whole.

I cracked but didn’t break, though my resolve was thin, 
For resilience is a fire that grows from within. 

They said I’d never rise from the ruins I knew, 
But I built myself anew, brick by aching brick. 
The thunder once feared me, now it fades in the blue
A shadow of doubt I outgrew, I outgrew. 

Now the sun finds me blooming where the fractures let light in, 
A testament to the grit that refused to submit. 
No tempest can sever the roots I’ve grown deep
For every heart that persists, love will always keep. 

So if you’re weathering battles, let your spirit be bold, 
The storm is just passing; you’ll be told and retold: 
That the mightiest oaks from the wildest seeds spring, 
And resilience, my darling, is the will to keep everything.
